name: gibbs_gibbs
provenance: meta-learner gap: gibbs_color_sweep → gibbs_color_sweep adjacent 236x in top solutions
idea: Fuse `gibbs_color_sweep` and `gibbs_color_sweep` into one operator. Evidence: gibbs_color_sweep→gibbs_color_sweep is the most frequent transition in the best solutions (236x); a fused operator bridging them may capture the effect in one cheaper step
math:
Let S be the spin state and ΔE_v the local field of variable v.
Phase 1 applies the acceptance rule of `gibbs_color_sweep` to propose a move set M;
Phase 2 immediately applies the update rule of `gibbs_color_sweep` RESTRICTED to the
neighborhood N(M) of variables touched in Phase 1, instead of a full pass.
The fused kernel therefore computes ΔE once per touched edge and reuses it
across both phases, which the two-operator sequence cannot.
pseudocode:
for sweep in 0..sweeps:
    M ← gibbs_color_sweep(S, T)              # phase 1: proposal/thermal pass
    for v in neighborhood(M):  # phase 2 fused on the touched region
        S ← gibbs_color_sweep_step(S, v)
    record observables
properties: strictly cheaper than the sequence `gibbs_color_sweep → gibbs_color_sweep` (shared ΔE, one memory pass)
same fixed points as the two-operator sequence
deterministic given (seed, sweep order) — required by the Harness Checker
complexity: O(|E|) per sweep (one pass over all edges)
status: DRAFT — no implementation exists. Per Stage 6 policy the platform never generates operator code; implementation requires human review and the full verification track.
